C1.why: Medi was interrupted by connection issues before finishing a sentence, not an actual error.

C2.why: Medi used the masculine adjective عيان for his fiancée, and Amal recast it to feminine عيانة.

C3.why: Medi produced an awkward word order هي بيوجع راسها, and Amal recast it to هي راسها بيوجع.

C4.why: Amal only asked if he was done, and Medi self-corrected the time without tutor correction.

C5.why: Medi was openly asking how to express the word rather than making an unprompted error.

C6.why: Medi was asking whether بنقلق was the right word, which is asking for vocabulary rather than a slip.

C7.why: Medi self-corrected from قلقان to the plural قلقانين before Amal spoke.

C8.why: Medi used the wrong preposition لـ with قلقان, and Amal corrected him to من.

C9.why: Medi was guessing a word he did not know and Amal set it aside without supplying the target form.

C10.why: Medi omitted the possessive suffix on بال and the preposition على, which Amal recast.

C11.why: Medi omitted على after بدير بالي, and Amal explicitly stated the rule that it takes على.

C12.why: Medi produced the malformed pronoun ending باليك, which Amal recast to بالك.

C13.why: Medi used past-tense عملنا after خلينا, and Amal immediately corrected it to bare present نعمل.

C14.why: Medi was asking for a word he did not know rather than making a statement error.

C15.why: غيم is a valid collective noun in Arabic, and Amal merely prompted him to supply the countable plural.

C16.why: Duplicate of C15 and not an actual lexical error.

C17.why: A comprehension misunderstanding of Amal's Arabic question in English is not a student speech slip.

C18.why: Medi was guessing and asking whether the word had to do with Azan.

C19.why: Medi explicitly stated he forgot the word and asked whether it was سجر or فجر.

C20.why: Medi incorrectly added لو to غير, and Amal explicitly rejected لو.

C21.why: Medi put el- on the noun after غير, and Amal recast it without el- and confirmed the rule.

C22.why: Medi was asking a question about the plural form rather than making an assertion slip.

C23.why: Medi used unnatural phrasing and word order in في الليل سما, which Amal recast to السما بالليل.

C24.why: Medi shifted from indefinite to definite القمر in an existential phrase, and Amal recast it back to indefinite قمر.

C25.why: Medi used masculine تاني with feminine نجمة, and Amal prompted him until he fixed it to تانية.

C26.why: Medi omitted the object pointer pronoun on بشوف, and Amal prompted him to point it back.

C27.why: Medi was asking how to say 'since' in Arabic.

C28.why: Medi asked a direct question about the verb form rather than making a slip.

C29.why: This was a tongue-tied stumble and stutter rather than a distinct grammar slip.

C30.why: Medi accidentally said الأول instead of الهوا, which Amal recast.

C31.why: Medi used the preposition من with غير, and Amal corrected it to عن.

C32.why: Medi added el- to مرة after آخر, and Amal explained the rule and gave the correct form آخر مرة.

C33.why: Medi used masculine كان with feminine مرة, and Amal prompted him until he fixed it to كانت.

C34.why: Medi said ثلاث سنين الماضي for 'three years ago', and Amal explicitly rejected it and taught قبل ثلاث سنين.

C35.why: Medi said سنان (teeth) instead of سنين (years), and Amal prompted him to correct the word.

C36.why: Medi used the incorrect past-tense verb form تلجات, and Amal recast it as تَلَّجَت.

C37.why: Amal was questioning the lexical choice of using 'came' for wind rather than correcting verb agreement; see C38.

C38.why: Medi said the wind 'came a lot', and Amal redirected him to express it as 'was very strong' (كان قوي).

C39.why: Duplicate candidate for the same corrected moment as C38.

C40.why: Medi switched to English with 'me' and asked if it was correct, which counts as code-switching/asking rather than a slip.

C41.why: Medi omitted the object pronoun on nadafet, and Amal prompted 'It.' until he added -ha.

C42.why: Amal merely asked a conversational clarifying question, not correcting an erroneous form.

C43.why: Medi was asking how to say plants rather than making a statement slip.

C44.why: Asked for the Arabic word for dirt, Medi incorrectly offered رمل (sand), which Amal rejected.

C45.why: Medi omitted el- on the adjective إدام after definite الشوارع, which Amal recast to الإدام.

C46.why: Medi translated 'made with stone' literally as عملت مع حجر, and Amal corrected it to a nominal sentence with حجر.

C47.why: Medi switched from his correct تاني حجر to حجر تاني ('another stone'), and Amal corrected him back to تاني حجر.

C48.why: Medi tried attaching a possessive pronoun to مفضل, and Amal corrected it to المفضل عندي.

C49.why: Medi placed the adjective before the noun (الـ مفضل حجر), and Amal corrected the word order.

C50.why: Medi added el- to a noun with a possessive suffix (الـ حجري), and Amal explicitly corrected 'No ال first'.

C51.why: Medi omitted el- on مفضل modifying definite الدرس, and Amal corrected it to المفضل عندي.

C52.why: Medi was asking a question to confirm whether إلي or عندي was appropriate.

C53.why: Medi used في as a copula 'is' in مش فيهن, and Amal explained that في means 'there is' and corrected to مش هون.

C54.why: Duplicate of C53, which is fundamentally a grammar copula slip rather than a vocabulary slip.

C55.why: Medi mangled the farewell into عافيا فيكي, and Amal recast the fixed formula يعطيك العافية.
